descriptionChirho: Quantitative adjective indicating a large number or amount: many people, much wealth, numerous occurrences — Arabic كَثِير, Korean 많은, Swahili -engi/-ingi, Hindi बहुत, Spanish muchos/mucho.
Qualitative adjective indicating greatness in size, importance, intensity, or power — Arabic عَظِيم, Korean 큰/크다, Swahili -kubwa/mkubwa, Hindi बड़ा/बड़ी/महान, Spanish grande.
Adjective in construct state meaning 'abounding in, rich in, full of' when followed by a noun — Korean 풍성한, Spanish abundante-de, Arabic كَثِيرُ + genitive.
Adverbial/exclamatory use meaning 'enough! sufficient!' — Arabic كَفَى/كَفَاكُمْ, Korean 족하다/충분하다, Swahili -tosha, Spanish basta/suficiente.
Comparative sense meaning 'more numerous, greater' — Arabic أَكْثَرُ/كَبِيرٌ, Korean 큰 것이, Spanish mayor/más.
Substantival noun רַב used as a title meaning 'chief, captain, master, great one' — Arabic رَئِيس, Korean 장관, Swahili mkuu, Hindi प्रधान.
Adverbial use indicating degree ('greatly') or temporal/spatial extent ('long, far') — Korean 크게/오래, Swahili sana/muda mrefu, Spanish grandemente/largo, Arabic طَوِيل.
Verbal forms (Qal perfect/conjunctive) meaning 'to become many, to increase, to multiply' — Arabic يَكثُرُ/تَكثُرَ/اِزْدَادَ, Korean 많아지다/커졌다, Swahili kuongezeka.
Noun form meaning 'abundance, multitude, greatness' used in construct or with prepositions — Arabic كَثْرَة, Korean 많음/큰, Swahili wingi/ukubwa.
Qal participle used as a substantive meaning 'defender, advocate, one who contends' — likely homographic with root ריב — Arabic مُحَامِي, Korean 싸우는 자, Swahili mtetezi.
